prompt.context: Your consulting firm has been hired by Durawear, a boots company in Spain. Your case leader wants you to crunch some numbers and present some findings to him.
prompt.question: Use the following data to: (1) Calculate the market size for each of the work boot and casual boot segments. (2) Calculate the total revenue and profit earned by Durawear in work boot and casual boot products. (3) Determine which segment is most important to Durawear and why.

clarifying_info.a: Durawear manufactures both work boots and casual boots and supplies to three customer segments: Laborers (blue collar workers), Executives (white collar workers), and Students.

clarifying_info.q: How many pairs does each segment buy per year?
clarifying_info.a: Laborers buy 2 pairs of work boots per year; all other segments (Executives and Students) purchase only one pair per year.
Durawear charges 150 Euros per pair of work boots and 100 Euros per pair of casual boots.

clarifying_info.q: What is the expected market growth?
clarifying_info.a: The work boot market is expected to grow at 5% per annum through 2012 and the casual boot market is expected to grow at 12.5% per annum through 2012.

exhibits.title: Market Share of Work and Casual by Competitor
exhibits.shows: Grouped bar chart showing percentage market share for Work Boots and Casual Boots across five competitors: Woodlands, Durawear, Steeler, Trekker, and Others.

exhibits.title: Male population segments (12+ age)
exhibits.shows: Grouped bar chart showing the percentage of each population segment that bought work boots vs. casual boots in the past year, alongside a table with the absolute population (in millions) for Laborers, Executives, and Students.

exhibits.title: Cost analysis
exhibits.shows: Stacked 100% bar chart showing cost and margin breakdown as a percentage of revenue for Durawear-Work boots, Durawear-Casual boots, and Woodlands, across seven cost categories: Materials, Labor, Sales & Marketing, Design, General admin, Retailer Margin, and Company margin.

framework: Estimate total market size for each segment (work and casual) by combining population data, purchase rates, purchase frequency, and price
Calculate Durawear's revenue in each segment using its market share
Calculate Durawear's profit using the company margin from the cost analysis exhibit
Compare segments on revenue, profit, margin, and growth rate to determine strategic priority
Recommend a differentiated strategy (defensive vs. aggressive) based on competitive position and profitability
Consider competitor behavior and Durawear's internal capabilities

questions.prompt: Calculate the total market size (in Euros) for the work boot segment across all three customer segments.
questions.guidance: Multiply each segment's population by its purchase rate, purchase frequency (Laborers buy 2 pairs/year, others buy 1), and the price of 150 Euros. Sum across all three segments.

math.setup: Market size per segment = Population (MM) x % buying work boots x pairs/year x price per pair
math.answer: Total work boot market size ≈ 2,605 million Euros

questions.prompt: Calculate the total market size (in Euros) for the casual boot segment across all three customer segments.
questions.guidance: Use the casual boot purchase rates from Exhibit 2, all segments buy 1 pair per year, at 100 Euros per pair.

math.setup: Market size per segment = Population (MM) x % buying casual boots x 1 pair/year x 100 Euros
math.answer: Total casual boot market size ≈ 1,025 million Euros

questions.prompt: Calculate Durawear's total revenue and profit for each product segment.
questions.guidance: Apply Durawear's market share (from Exhibit 1) to the total market size for each segment to get revenue. Then apply the company margin percentage (from Exhibit 3) to get profit.

math.setup: Revenue = Total market size x Durawear market share; Profit = Revenue x Company margin %
steps: Work boots: Revenue = 2,605M x 16% = 416.8M Euros; Profit margin = 15%; Profit = 416.8M x 15% ≈ 60M Euros
Casual boots: Revenue = 1,025M x 40% = 410M Euros; Profit margin = 22%; Profit = 410M x 22% = 90.2M ≈ 90M Euros
math.answer: Work boots: Revenue ~417M Euros, Profit ~60M Euros. Casual boots: Revenue ~410M Euros, Profit ~90M Euros.

questions.prompt: Which product segment is most important to Durawear and why? What strategy should they follow for each segment?
questions.guidance: Despite similar revenues, casual boots generate higher absolute profit (90M vs. 60M) and a higher margin (22% vs. 15%). The casual boot market also grows faster (12.5% vs. 5% p.a.). A strong candidate will recommend a defensive strategy for work boots to protect existing share, and an aggressive growth strategy for casual boots. They should also note the need to assess competitor moves and Durawear's internal capabilities.

brainstorming.prompt: What other factors should Durawear consider when deciding how to allocate resources between work boots and casual boots?

categories.name: Competitor dynamics
ideas: Woodlands holds 43% of the casual boot market — a dominant position Durawear must overcome
Trekker holds 34% of work boots — Durawear's 16% share is vulnerable
Understanding competitor pricing and distribution strategies is essential

categories.name: Internal capabilities
ideas: Durawear's cost structure in work boots is less efficient (higher labor and S&M costs)
Casual boot margin of 22% vs. work boot margin of 15% suggests better operational fit
Assess whether design and manufacturing capabilities support casual boot expansion

categories.name: Market growth
ideas: Casual boot market growing at 12.5% p.a. vs. 5% for work boots through 2012
Higher growth in casual boots amplifies the value of gaining share now
Work boot market may commoditize over time

categories.name: Customer insight
ideas: Executives and Students drive casual boot demand — more brand-sensitive segments
Laborers are the core work boot buyers — relationship-driven, price-sensitive
Understanding repurchase loyalty and switching behavior matters

recommendation: Casual boots are the most important segment: higher profit (90M vs. 60M Euros), higher margin (22% vs. 15%), and faster market growth (12.5% vs. 5% p.a.).
Deploy an aggressive growth strategy in casual boots to capture share from dominant competitor Woodlands (43% share).
Deploy a defensive strategy in work boots to protect existing 16% share and maintain the 60M Euros profit contribution.
risks: Woodlands' dominant casual boot share (43%) will require significant investment to displace
Aggressive casual boot investment may dilute focus from the work boot base
Cost structure in work boots may erode margins further if not managed
next_steps: Analyze Woodlands' pricing, distribution, and brand positioning in casual boots
Assess Durawear's manufacturing and design capacity to scale casual boot production
Model the investment required to grow casual boot share by 5-10 percentage points and estimate ROI
